en: Jātaka:
The Second Book of Pairs (Dukanipāta), The Chapter on the Jackal (Siṅgālavagga)
10. The Kapi-jātaka:
“This seer, who delights in tranquility and self-restraint, stands here, distressed by the fear of the cold.”
"Come now, let us enter this little hut;
it will dispel all cold and distress.
"This seer does not delight in tranquility and self-restraint;"
"This monkey, whose domain is the branches of the best of trees,
is a defiler and a provoker;
he might even defile my very own dwelling."
The Kapi Jātaka is the tenth.
The tenth chapter, the Siṅgāla Vagga.
Its summary verse (uddāna):
Then King Siṅgālavara, the dog,
and likewise Kosiya, the eater of raw flesh,
as well as Dānavarottha, by means of the charioteer—
And the Punabbasuka, the Sīsapā, and the Kapi—these are ten.
Now, the summary of the chapters (vagga-uddāna):
The Daḷha chapter, and after that the Santhava.
And a *rūhaka* like the *kalyāṇavagga*;
furthermore, a *nataṃdaḷha*, a *bīraṇa*-thicket,
a *kāsāva*, a sandal, and one bitten by a jackal.
The Second Book is finished.
